findings.F1: Step 5 found no grading and no mean effect. The slope of the 5-day drift-adjusted return on the short's size is -0.00033 (t -0.73, 1648 cases). The unusual move per case is +0.10 %, on the wrong side of the short, with t 0.22 over 588 days and a strength of 0.011. In folds B and C the recorded forecast's slope at 5 days is +0.000078 (t 0.12, 773 cases).
findings.F2: Calmness does not grade the fall at 5 days. By size-of-short quintile, the drift-adjusted 5-day means are -1.9 % for the smallest shorts (t -2.28), then -0.3 %, then +1.0 %, then -0.6 % for the largest (309 cases). The calmest declines fall no more than the least calm.
findings.F3: The effect is mixed across windows, and the clear ones point against the idea. Window slopes at 5 days have t +3.40 (w17), +2.48 (w18) and +2.26 (w15), against -1.94 (w10). The rest lie between -0.7 and +1.7, so no period carries a continuation.
findings.F4: No coin shows it either. The 5-day slopes by coin have t from -0.90 (XMR) to +0.47 (ZEC), and XRP points the wrong way at t +2.21.
findings.F5: Depth does not locate the effect. Inside the deeper and the shallower halves of the 28-day falls, the calmness slope has t +0.48 and -0.28 at 5 days, and +0.49 and -0.47 at 10 days. By 28-day-fall quintile, the 5-day means are not monotone: +0.3 %, -1.9 %, -2.4 %, -1.1 % and +1.5 % from deepest to shallowest.
findings.F6: Another horizon does not reveal it cleanly. At 10 days the slope on the size of the short has t -0.02 (380 cases), and at 20 days t -0.94 (195 cases). Only the unstandardised ratio reaches t -2.25 at 20 days, on 195 cases that fall on just 54 days and with no day grouping. The mean drift-adjusted move in the regime has day-grouped t of -0.60, -0.51 and +0.22 at 5, 10 and 20 days.

no_ideas: The tested effect is zero rather than short of the bar: an unusual move of +0.10 % with t 0.22, and a slope t of -0.73. No coin, window, depth or horizon shows calm declines falling more in a way that holds up (F1–F6), so neither more data nor a narrowed version is supported.
